ECAB executive attention card sort (a child adaptation of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test), given by a research assistant: the child finds the teddy bear's preferred balloon by colour, then a changed colour, then shape, up to 20 trials per stage, six consecutive correct to pass, stopped at a failed stage (Samson et al. 2021, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0257877). The released WSCT ('Executive attention score (/60)', observed 12-60, 7 missing) is not the 0-3 stages score the paper describes; it falls with age and with the other ECAB scores and clusters at 18 (6 + 6 + 6) and 32 (6 + 6 + 20), so it is read as trials used, a failed or unreached stage counting 20, and reversed as 60 - WSCT so that higher = better. Partial: scoring undocumented and direction inferred from the data; one released 12, below the 18 minimum that reading allows, is set to NA.
